text:
scan-bot: :rotating_light: Leakage detected by external-monitor: public GitHub gist contains possible EMBED_SERVICE_KEY for 'embed-service'. gist: https://gist.github.com/xxxx (automated confidence: 0.92).

alex: seeing it, opening thread. gist snippet shows `EMBED_SERVICE_KEY=sk-live-3f7a9b...` (not posting full key here).

maria: yikes. do we know if that key maps to a customer workspace or internal infra?

sanjay: running quick audit now. query: `SELECT count(1) FROM token_usage WHERE key_hash = 'sha256:8f3a...' AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days';`

sanjay: result -> 0 rows. (looks like it hasn't been used in 30d)

security-oncall: regardless, treat as compromised. Plan: 1) revoke key 2) create replacement via KMS + SecretsManager 3) rotate any deployments that reference it 4) scan additional repos/gists 5) update runbook + notify infra owners.

ops: ready to revoke once we have the token id. alex, can you grep our secrets inventory to map the leaked value to an internal record (we store key hashes only)? sample command: `redis-cli HGET token:index sha256:8f3a...`

alex: ran the hash lookup. it maps to token id `tok-prod-embed-17`. env tag = `embed-service:ingest-prod`. created_by = `svc/ingest-runner`. scope = embeddings:write. created_at = 2024-11-02.

maria: is that used by any customer-facing pipeline? ingest-prod handles customer uploads for embeddings — potential blast radius. need containment fast.

security-oncall: revoke now. ops, run `redwoodctl tokens revoke --id=tok-prod-embed-17 --reason "leaked in public gist"` and confirm. also create a new key: `redwoodctl tokens create --scope embeddings:write --kms redwood-kms-prod --notes "rotate after leak 1752467890"`

ops: running revoke...

ops: revoke returned 200 OK. token state = revoked. rotated: new_token_id = tok-prod-embed-98. new token created under KMS alias `redwood-kms-prod`. storing secret in SM under `/prod/tokens/embed/ingest-prod`.

alex: updating all deployment configs that reference old token: CI secrets + helm values. pushing change to staging first.

devex: add note — we should update local quickstart and any public examples to ensure no sample keys are left in docs. also add a pre-receive hook to block `EMBED_SERVICE_KEY=` patterns on pushes to main.

maria: audit check: searching usage logs for client IPs / unusual calls from that token in the last 90 days. query: `SELECT ts, src_ip, route FROM requests WHERE token_id = 'tok-prod-embed-17' AND ts >= now() - interval '90 days' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 100;`

maria: results -> 0 rows. seems not used. good sign.

security-oncall: we still need to treat as incident. Actions: - escalate to legal if gist contains customer data - check S3 access logs for related object reads - push block on GitHub user if they're within org scope - run full repo/gist sweep for similar patterns.

alex: ran a quick sweep across our public repos and gists: found 2 more small gists with base64 blobs that look like old sandbox keys (rotated long ago). flagged and removed.

ops: changed ingestion service secrets in k8s: `kubectl -n embed set secret embed-ingest --from-literal=EMBED_SERVICE_KEY=<redacted-new>` and restarted deployments with rolling restart. health checks green.

security-oncall: update audit logging: ensure token revocation events are logged in audit stream and forwarded to splunk/alerts. also add an automated check to compare public leak scanner hits with token inventory to auto-open incidents.

devex: created GH pre-receive rule draft and a repo policy PR: block base64 blobs over 200 chars and token-looking patterns. also will add instructions for developers to use `redwoodctl tokens create --kms` in dev onboarding.

maria: any customer comms needed? since token had no usage, recommend internal-only notification. if legal disagrees we'll escalate.

security-oncall: agree. timeline: detection -> revoke -> rotate -> config update -> repo sweep -> rules added. create post-incident ticket with timeline and follow-ups: (1) enable enforced KMS use for prod tokens (2) add DLP/gist monitoring to our SCRM rules (3) webhook to auto-revoke exposed tokens older than 90 days.

alex: filing JIRA: INFSEC-3442 "Public gist leaked embed service token — rotate + harden" with checklist. assigning to ops + devex + security-oncall.

ops: checklist completed for immediate items, leaving follow-ups in the ticket.

security-oncall: postmortem draft will include root cause: token credential accidentally copied into a personal gist by svc account owner while debugging; corrective: update runbook + require `redwoodctl` for creating prod tokens (disabled raw keys in console).

maria: thanks everyone. closing incident thread once doc + postmortem uploaded to confluence. :white_check_mark: 

alex: uploaded artifacts (revoke logs, audit queries, gist screenshots) to the ticket. marking thread resolved."
